affects.why: A Republican sweep would push yields and the dollar up and gold down; a slow count could lift gold as a haven (FXStreet, Admirals).
In a disputed result, high-beta tech would take the brunt; a Democratic House brings data-centre regulation risk (TradingKey).

downside: A Republican sweep is the 'unpriced' risk: higher long yields and dollar, lower gold (FXStreet).
A slow or disputed count would hit high-beta tech hardest (TradingKey).

result.headline: Democrats win the House and are projected to take the Senate; Nasdaq-100 futures fell as much as 2.2% then narrowed to about -0.6%
points: Democrats won the House (projected 235-252 seats) and at least 51 Senate seats after flipping six, including Texas and Ohio (Pomegra).
That was the 'blue sweep', which prediction markets had seen as likely for the House but closer for the Senate.
Tech fell hardest overnight on fears of tighter data-centre rules: Nvidia about -1.5%, Amazon lower (Yahoo/Stocktwits).
Dollar and US yields fell, gold rose 0.5% (Reuters) - mixed for your pie: SGLN up, but a firmer pound trims the sterling value of US holdings.
Analysts expect hearings and investigations more than laws that stop data-centre building (Reuters, Stifel).

upside: A split Congress: 'gridlock is Goldilocks' for shares (BofA's Hartnett).

A tighter budget could ease pressure to hike, softening the pound (Admirals).

upside: A hike with hawkish guidance could take GBP/USD through 1.3408 towards 1.35 (Tradingnews).

upside: A weak number would lower the odds of the December Fed hike; falling December odds support gold and shares (Admirals).

A preview says the report must show whether softer Texas (ERCOT) power prices have stopped eating into the 2027 outlook, and that investors want a first customer for its Helix data-centre platform.

TradingKey points to AWS revenue up 39% to $46bn and Google Cloud up 103% to $30.7bn last quarter, and says Meta's $15bn five-part bond sale on 3 Nov eased worries about funding its AI build-out. sources.title: Analysis: Trump's midterm drubbing demonstrates the power of data center opponents

stories.summary: Nvidia lagged the rebound, closing 3.1% lower, as chip and data-centre stocks sold off on fears that new state governments will slow AI building. Reuters reports Goldman Sachs sees roughly 45% of planned US data-centre capacity at risk from moratoria, tighter rules or smaller tax breaks after Democratic wins in Texas, Michigan and Georgia. Morgan Stanley sees a significant risk of delay for a 10-gigawatt Ohio project involving Nvidia.

JPMorgan raised its target to $5.10 from $4.80 and kept Overweight; Barclays earlier trimmed its target to $4. The shares had traded around $2.70-3.00 for weeks before the report.

Amazon is named alongside Google and Microsoft as facing scrutiny of AI spending [2].

Reuters says Korea's Kospi fell 4.8% and Taiwan 2.6%, while TradingKey reported SK Hynix down 6.1%, Samsung down 3.4% and Kioxia down 8.4%. Japan's Nikkei held up better.

Qualcomm slides 7% on a soft outlook as a memory squeeze hits phones and its $5 billion data center bet takes center stage

stories.summary: Qualcomm beat on Q4 revenue ($10.44bn) but guided EPS slightly below forecasts as a global memory shortage hits phone sales; it expects about $5bn of data-centre revenue in fiscal 2027 and says supply, not demand, is the limit. Optical-parts maker Coherent rose about 5% after hours on strong guidance tied to AI data-centre demand, and AppLovin jumped about 21%.

explainer.meaning: A temporary official ban on new projects, here on connecting new data centres to the grid while rules are reviewed.

stories.headline: Voters turn on data centres: Goldman sees ~45% of planned US capacity at risk

impacts.why: Vistra named among power firms that slumped on the result [1].

sources.title: Analysis: Trump's midterm drubbing demonstrates the power of data center opponents

stories.summary: A Reuters analysis says data-centre opposition helped decide races in Texas, Georgia and Ohio, with critics arguing the sites push up power bills and create too few jobs. Texas holds about a quarter of US data-centre capacity due by 2030 and Atlanta is the busiest construction market. Power firms GE Vernova, Constellation and Vistra slumped, as did data-centre hosts Core Scientific (-11.6%) and Iren (-12.5%).

explainer.meaning: Gold pays no interest, so it tends to do better when bond yields fall and you give up less by holding it.

Yields at a two-month low and a weaker dollar [2].

stories.summary: Spot gold rose about $146 (3.7%) to roughly $4,065 an ounce on Wednesday and silver gained 5%, as the dollar fell to a one-month low and oil slumped. Reuters says Treasury yields dropped to a two-month low overnight, which lowers the cost of holding gold.

explainer.meaning: When the White House and Congress are controlled by different parties, so few big new laws pass; markets often like the predictability.

Reuters' Morning Bid says investors expect a divided Washington to be good for markets, alongside hopes for an end to the eight-month Middle East war. Hong Kong (+1.7%) and Shanghai (+2.2%) rose overnight while Korea fell.

sources.title: Bank of England preview: first hike to 4% expected as energy pushes inflation to 3.5%

stories.summary: The Bank of England is widely expected to lift Bank Rate from 3.75% to 4% at 12:00 UK today, with new forecasts in its Monetary Policy Report. UK inflation rose to 3.5% in September, mostly on fuel costs; Goldman expects a 7-2 vote and forecasts inflation peaking above 4% early next year. Analysts say the vote split and guidance will matter more for the pound and gilts than the hike itself.

explainer.meaning: The main global benchmark price for oil, used to price most of the world's crude.

Treasury yields fell to a two-month low and the dollar weakened against most currencies, leaving sterling near a seven-week high ahead of the Bank of England.
